```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
```

## Goal

The clocks are applied to bulk tumor RNA-seq, and a bulk tumor sample mixes
malignant cells with the patient's own stroma and immune cells. A reader will
ask whether the age-matched deviations, the pathway contributions, and the
clinical associations in the main figures are driven by how much tumor is in
each sample rather than by tumor biology. This script answers that with the
TCGA ABSOLUTE purity estimates.

Everything here reads from objects the main pipeline already saved. Nothing
is recomputed and no clock is refit. Where a main-figure analysis is
repeated with purity added, the model form, data filters, and contrasts
follow the figure script.

**What is asked, and why**

1. *Does deviation track purity, in each of the six cancers?* If the
   youth-like state lives in malignant cells, deviation should become more
   youth-like as purity rises, because non-malignant tissue at the patient's
   age sits near the age expectation and dilutes the signal. The size of the
   effect also says how much of the tumor-to-tumor spread purity explains.
2. *Does purity confound the deviation-survival associations?* The
   cross-cancer survival panel reports deviation against overall survival in
   each cancer. Purity could be prognostic itself, so each model is refit
   with purity added.
3. *In BRCA, which pathway contributions track purity?* The BRCA figures
   describe the pathway structure of the deviation. Purity could act through
   particular pathways (for example immune programs) rather than scaling
   everything equally.
4. *In BRCA, do the subtype, survival, and TP53 results hold with purity in
   the model?* These are the main-text claims that could be confounded:
   subtype ordering, the deviation-survival association (the forest in the
   survival figure), and the truncating-TP53 effect on the P53-pathway
   contribution, which is a purity-correlated outcome.

**What this script produces**

Four panels, each drawn in the style of the corresponding main panel so the
two can be compared directly: deviation against purity in six cancers; BRCA
deviation by PAM50 subtype after purity adjustment; the BRCA TP53 panel with
purity in the model; and the BRCA overall-survival forest with purity in the
model. One table: the cross-cancer survival models without and with purity,
on the tumors with a purity value. Some panels may not appear in the
published manuscript. Panels are assembled and typeset in Adobe Illustrator.
The remaining tables and the pathway analysis stay in this report as the
record.

**Data**

Deviations and contributions come from the saved ClockSHAP objects
(`clockshap_objects-<feature_set>.rds`), exactly as used in the figures.
Purity is the PanCancerAtlas ABSOLUTE estimate from the harmonized TCGA
metadata, one value per patient, joined on the 12-character patient barcode.
Patients with more than one tumor profile keep all profiles, each carrying the
patient's purity, so the tumor set matches the main figures. Overall survival
and TP53 mutation calls come from the same files the figure scripts use.
Tumors without a purity value are dropped only where purity enters a model.
SCAN-B has no purity estimate, so the BRCA analyses are TCGA only.


## Cancers of interest

The six emphasis cancers, each paired with its GTEx tissue of origin.

```{r}
map <- list(
  BRCA = "BREAST",
  LUSC = "LUNG",
  LUAD = "LUNG",
  GBM  = "BRAIN",
  LGG  = "BRAIN",
  COAD = "COLON"
)
```

## Load purity

One row per patient; the join below relies on that.

```{r}
harmonized <- readRDS(params$purity_rds)

stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(harmonized$submitter_id))
stopifnot(all(nchar(harmonized$submitter_id) == 12))

purity_by_patient <- setNames(as.numeric(harmonized$purity), harmonized$submitter_id)

msg("Harmonized metadata: ", length(purity_by_patient), " patients, ",
    sum(!is.na(purity_by_patient)), " with a purity value.")
```

## Assemble the tumor table

For each cancer: read the saved ClockSHAP object and sample metadata, check
that the decomposition still closes and that every tumor has metadata, bridge
to the patient barcode, and attach purity. PAM50 is carried for BRCA only,
and the BRCA contribution matrix is kept for the pathway analyses.

```{r}
suffix       <- paste0("-", params$feature_set)
out_root_abs <- here::here(params$out_root)

sample_list <- list()
phi_brca    <- NULL

for (tcga in names(map)) {
  gtex        <- map[[tcga]]
  analysis_id <- paste0(tcga, "__", gtex)
  adir        <- file.path(out_root_abs, analysis_id)

  cs   <- readRDS(file.path(adir, paste0("clockshap_objects", suffix, ".rds")))
  meta <- readRDS(file.path(adir, "sample_metadata.rds"))

  phi <- as.matrix(cs$pt$phi)
  ids <- rownames(phi)
  dev <- as.numeric(cs$pt$deviation)

  # the contributions must still sum to the deviation, and every tumor must have metadata
  stopifnot(length(dev) == nrow(phi))
  stopifnot(max(abs(rowSums(phi) - dev)) < 1e-8)
  stopifnot(all(ids %in% rownames(meta)))

  barcode <- as.character(meta[ids, "tcga.tcga_barcode"])
  patient <- substr(barcode, 1, 12)

  sample_list[[tcga]] <- tibble(
    sample_id = ids,
    cancer    = tcga,
    tissue    = gtex,
    patient   = patient,
    barcode   = barcode,
    age_years = as.numeric(meta[ids, "age_years"]),
    deviation = dev,
    purity    = unname(purity_by_patient[patient]),
    pam50     = if (tcga == "BRCA") as.character(meta[ids, "Subtype_Selected"]) else NA_character_
  )

  if (tcga == "BRCA") phi_brca <- phi

  msg(analysis_id, ": ", length(ids), " tumors, ",
      sum(!is.na(sample_list[[tcga]]$purity)), " with purity.")
}

samples <- dplyr::bind_rows(sample_list) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cancer = factor(cancer, levels = names(map)))

# purity is a fraction; anything outside [0, 1] would mean a wrong column or join
stopifnot(all(is.na(samples$purity) | (samples$purity >= 0 & samples$purity <= 1)))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(phi_brca), samples$sample_id[samples$cancer == "BRCA"]))
```

## Load overall survival

The same clinical resource and join as the survival figures: one clinical
row per patient, attached to every tumor profile of that patient. Tumors are
kept where time, event, and age are available.

```{r}
clinical <- utils::read.csv(
  params$clinical_csv,
  na.strings       = c("NA", "", "#N/A"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
  check.names      = TRUE
)

clin2 <- clinical %>%
  dplyr::mutate(patient = substr(as.character(bcr_patient_barcode), 1, 12)) %>%
  dplyr::distinct(patient, .keep_all = TRUE) %>%
  dplyr::select(patient, OS.time, OS)

samples <- samples %>%
  dplyr::left_join(clin2, by = "patient") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    os_time  = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(OS.time)),
    os_event = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(OS)) == 1
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(-OS.time, -OS)

os_eligible <- is.finite(samples$os_time) & !is.na(samples$os_event) & is.finite(samples$age_years)
msg("OS-eligible tumors: ", sum(os_eligible), " of ", nrow(samples))
```

## Shared helpers

```{r}
# Cox hazard ratio for one term; `scale` rescales the coefficient (0.1 gives HR per 10 percentage points)
cox_term <- function(df, formula_str, term_name, scale = 1) {
  fit <- survival::coxph(stats::as.formula(formula_str), data = df)
  co  <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  stopifnot(term_name %in% rownames(co))
  tibble(
    HR      = exp(scale * co[term_name, "coef"]),
    CI_low  = exp(scale * (co[term_name, "coef"] - 1.96 * co[term_name, "se(coef)"])),
    CI_high = exp(scale * (co[term_name, "coef"] + 1.96 * co[term_name, "se(coef)"])),
    p_value = co[term_name, "Pr(>|z|)"]
  )
}

# Linear-model coefficient for one term, with CI; `scale` as above
lm_term <- function(fit, term_name, scale = 1) {
  co <- summary(fit)$coefficients
  ci <- stats::confint(fit)
  stopifnot(term_name %in% rownames(co))
  tibble(
    estimate = scale * co[term_name, "Estimate"],
    CI_low   = scale * ci[term_name, 1],
    CI_high  = scale * ci[term_name, 2],
    p_value  = co[term_name, "Pr(>|t|)"]
  )
}

pam50_levels <- c("Normal-Like", "LumA", "LumB", "Her2", "Basal")
harmonize_pam50 <- function(x) {
  factor(dplyr::recode(as.character(x), "Normal" = "Normal-Like"), levels = pam50_levels)
}

# palettes shared with the main figures
pam50_pal <- c(
  "Normal-Like" = "#cccccc",
  "LumA"        = "#4575b4",
  "LumB"        = "#91bfdb",
  "Her2"        = "#fc8d59",
  "Basal"       = "#d73027"
)
hr_pal <- c(
  '"youth-like" deviation, increased risk'      = "#2c7bb6",
  'less "youth-like" deviation, increased risk' = "#d7191c"
)

theme_supp <- function(base_size = 10) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold"),
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA)
    )
}
```

# Analysis 1 — Deviation against purity, six cancers

**Question.** Does age-matched deviation change with tumor purity, and how
much of the spread among tumors does purity explain?

**Why.** If the youth-like state is carried by malignant cells, the measured
deviation should scale with the malignant fraction, because non-malignant
tissue at the patient's age sits near the age expectation. A negative slope
is the expected signature of that dilution. The R-squared gain says how much
tumor-to-tumor variance purity accounts for beyond chronological age, which
is separate from whether it explains the mean shift.

**How.** Per cancer: Spearman correlation between deviation and purity, and
`deviation ~ age + purity`. The slope is reported per 10 percentage points of
purity so it reads in years. `r2_purity_given_age` is the R-squared of the
full model minus that of `deviation ~ age`.

```{r}
dev_purity <- purity_data$samples %>%
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(purity))

dev_rows <- list()

for (tcga in levels(dev_purity$cancer)) {
  d <- dplyr::filter(dev_purity, cancer == tcga)

  ct       <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(d$deviation, d$purity, method = "spearman"))
  fit_age  <- stats::lm(deviation ~ age_years,          data = d)
  fit_full <- stats::lm(deviation ~ age_years + purity, data = d)
  slope    <- lm_term(fit_full, "purity", scale = 0.1)

  dev_rows[[tcga]] <- tibble(
    cancer              = tcga,
    n                   = nrow(d),
    purity_range        = sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(d$purity), max(d$purity)),
    spearman_rho        = unname(ct$estimate),
    spearman_p          = ct$p.value,
    slope_per_10pct     = slope$estimate,
    ci_low              = slope$CI_low,
    ci_high             = slope$CI_high,
    lm_p                = slope$p_value,
    r2_purity_given_age = summary(fit_full)$r.squared - summary(fit_age)$r.squared
  )
}

dev_purity_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(dev_rows) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cancer = factor(cancer, levels = names(map)))

knitr::kable(
  dev_purity_tbl, digits = 3,
  caption = "Deviation against ABSOLUTE purity per cancer. Spearman is unadjusted; the slope and CI are from deviation ~ age + purity, per 10 percentage points of purity."
)
```

Scatter per cancer with an unadjusted linear fit and the Spearman
correlation in each panel. The slope and R-squared gain stay in the table
above as the record.
Dashed line: the GTEx age expectation (deviation of zero).

```{r, fig.width=7.5, fig.height=5}
dev_labels <- dev_purity_tbl %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("rho = %.2f, %s", spearman_rho,
                                ifelse(spearman_p < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", spearman_p))))

p_dev_purity <- ggplot(dev_purity, aes(x = purity, y = deviation)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, size = 0.9, colour = "grey30") +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x, se = TRUE, colour = "#d7191c", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text(data = dev_labels, aes(x = Inf, y = Inf, label = label),
            hjust = 1.05, vjust = 1.3, size = 3, colour = "grey20", inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ cancer, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.25))) +   # headroom for the annotation
  labs(x = "Tumor purity (ABSOLUTE)", y = "Age-matched deviation (years)") +
  theme_supp()

p_dev_purity
```

# Analysis 2 — Deviation and overall survival with purity, six cancers

**Question.** Do the cross-cancer deviation-survival associations change
when purity is in the model, and is purity itself prognostic?

**Why.** The cross-cancer survival panel fits `Surv ~ age + deviation` per
cancer. If purity predicts survival and also predicts deviation, the
deviation effect could be carried by purity. Refitting with purity added, on
the same tumors, tests that directly.

**How.** Three rows per cancer. The first reproduces the figure's model on
all OS-eligible tumors. The second and third use only tumors with a purity
value, without and with purity, so those two are compared on identical
tumors. HR is per one year of deviation. Purity's own HR is per 10
percentage points. When comparing the first row with the other two, the
estimate is the comparison; the p-value also moves with the sample size.

```{r}
surv_all <- purity_data$samples %>%
  dplyr::filter(is.finite(os_time), !is.na(os_event), is.finite(age_years))

surv_rows <- list()
pur_rows  <- list()

for (tcga in levels(surv_all$cancer)) {
  d_all <- dplyr::filter(surv_all, cancer == tcga)
  d_pur <- dplyr::filter(d_all, !is.na(purity))

  specs <- list(
    list(label = "age + deviation (all OS-eligible tumors)", data = d_all, f = "Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation"),
    list(label = "age + deviation (tumors with purity)",     data = d_pur, f = "Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation"),
    list(label = "age + deviation + purity",                 data = d_pur, f = "Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation + purity")
  )

  for (s in specs) {
    surv_rows[[paste(tcga, s$label)]] <- cox_term(s$data, s$f, "deviation") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(cancer = tcga, model = s$label, n = nrow(s$data), events = sum(s$data$os_event)) %>%
      dplyr::select(cancer, model, n, events, HR, CI_low, CI_high, p_value)
  }

  pur_rows[[tcga]] <- cox_term(d_pur, "Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation + purity", "purity", scale = 0.1) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(cancer = tcga, n = nrow(d_pur), events = sum(d_pur$os_event)) %>%
    dplyr::select(cancer, n, events, HR, CI_low, CI_high, p_value)
}

surv_purity_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(surv_rows) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(cancer = factor(cancer, levels = names(map)))

knitr::kable(
  surv_purity_tbl, digits = 4,
  caption = "Overall-survival hazard ratio per +1 year of deviation, by cancer, without and with purity in the model. Rows 2 and 3 of each cancer are fit on the same tumors."
)
```

The supplementary table: one row per cancer, the deviation hazard ratio
without and with purity on the tumors that have a purity value. The
figure's estimate on all OS-eligible tumors is already in the main survival
table and is not repeated; it stays in the record table above.

```{r}
fmt_hr <- function(hr, lo, hi) sprintf("%.3f (%.3f-%.3f)", hr, lo, hi)
fmt_pv <- function(p) ifelse(p < 0.001, "<0.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))

surv_purity_si_tbl <- surv_purity_tbl %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    column = dplyr::case_when(
      model == "age + deviation (all OS-eligible tumors)" ~ "figure",
      model == "age + deviation (tumors with purity)"     ~ "age",
      model == "age + deviation + purity"                 ~ "age_purity"
    ),
    hr_ci = fmt_hr(HR, CI_low, CI_high),
    p     = fmt_pv(p_value)
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(cancer, column, n, events, hr_ci, p) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = column, values_from = c(n, events, hr_ci, p)) %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    Cancer                                        = cancer,
    `Tumors (events)`                             = sprintf("%d (%d)", n_age, events_age),
    `HR per year, age-adjusted (95% CI)`          = hr_ci_age,
    `p`                                           = p_age,
    `HR per year, age + purity adjusted (95% CI)` = hr_ci_age_purity,
    `p `                                          = p_age_purity
  )

knitr::kable(
  surv_purity_si_tbl,
  caption = "Supplementary table: overall-survival hazard ratio per +1 year of age-matched deviation, by cancer, on the tumors with a purity value, from the age-adjusted model and from the same model with tumor purity added."
)
```

# BRCA — tumor table for the breast analyses

BRCA tumors with PAM50 relabelled as in the figures ("Normal" to
"Normal-Like"). Purity may be missing; each analysis below filters as it
needs.

```{r}
brca <- purity_data$samples %>%
  dplyr::filter(cancer == "BRCA") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pam50 = harmonize_pam50(pam50))

stopifnot(!anyNA(brca$pam50))
stopifnot(identical(rownames(purity_data$phi_brca), brca$sample_id))

brca_pur <- dplyr::filter(brca, !is.na(purity))
phi_b    <- purity_data$phi_brca[brca_pur$sample_id, , drop = FALSE]
retained <- colnames(phi_b)[colSums(abs(phi_b)) > 0]

msg("BRCA tumors: ", nrow(brca), "; with purity: ", nrow(brca_pur),
    "; retained pathways: ", length(retained))
```

---

# Analysis 3 — BRCA pathway contributions against purity

Kept in this report as the record (not used in the manuscript).

**Question.** Which pathway contributions track purity in BRCA, and are
they the same pathways that carry the mean youth-like shift?

**Why.** Purity could scale every contribution equally, or it could act
through particular programs. Immune and stromal Hallmark sets are expected
to depend on how much non-malignant tissue is in the sample; proliferative
programs are not. Comparing each pathway's cohort-mean contribution with its
purity dependence separates the two roles. PAM50 is the dominant source of
variation in BRCA, so each correlation is also computed within subtype.

**How.** BRCA tumors with purity, and the pathways the breast clock retained
(non-zero column). For each pathway: Spearman correlation between its
contribution and purity, raw, and the partial Spearman correlation after
regressing both the contribution and purity on PAM50. Total deviation is
included as a reference row. Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment is over the
pathways only.

```{r}
partial_spearman <- function(x, y, z) {
  rx <- stats::residuals(stats::lm(x ~ z))
  ry <- stats::residuals(stats::lm(y ~ z))
  ct <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(rx, ry, method = "spearman"))
  c(rho = unname(ct$estimate), p = ct$p.value)
}

path_rows <- list()

for (pw in c("Total deviation", retained)) {
  v   <- if (pw == "Total deviation") brca_pur$deviation else phi_b[, pw]
  raw <- suppressWarnings(stats::cor.test(v, brca_pur$purity, method = "spearman"))
  adj <- partial_spearman(v, brca_pur$purity, brca_pur$pam50)

  path_rows[[pw]] <- tibble(
    pathway       = pw,
    mean_phi      = mean(v),
    rho_raw       = unname(raw$estimate),
    p_raw         = raw$p.value,
    rho_pam50_adj = adj[["rho"]],
    p_pam50_adj   = adj[["p"]]
  )
}

phi_purity_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(path_rows)

is_pw <- phi_purity_tbl$pathway != "Total deviation"
phi_purity_tbl$p_raw_bh       <- NA_real_
phi_purity_tbl$p_pam50_adj_bh <- NA_real_
phi_purity_tbl$p_raw_bh[is_pw]       <- stats::p.adjust(phi_purity_tbl$p_raw[is_pw],       method = "BH")
phi_purity_tbl$p_pam50_adj_bh[is_pw] <- stats::p.adjust(phi_purity_tbl$p_pam50_adj[is_pw], method = "BH")

phi_purity_tbl <- phi_purity_tbl %>%
  dplyr::arrange(pathway != "Total deviation", dplyr::desc(abs(rho_raw)))

knitr::kable(
  phi_purity_tbl, digits = 3,
  caption = "BRCA pathway contributions against purity. rho_raw is the Spearman correlation; rho_pam50_adj is the partial Spearman correlation after regressing both variables on PAM50. BH adjustment is over the retained pathways."
)
```

## Overview: mean contribution beside purity correlation

Each retained pathway's mean contribution beside its purity correlation, in
the same order. A pathway with a large mean and near-zero correlation
carries the cohort shift regardless of purity; a pathway with a near-zero
mean and a large correlation moves individual tumors with purity but
averages out.

```{r, fig.width=8, fig.height=5.5}
phi_plot_df <- phi_purity_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(pathway != "Total deviation") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(pathway = factor(pathway, levels = pathway[order(mean_phi)])) %>%
  dplyr::select(pathway, `Mean contribution (years)` = mean_phi, `Spearman correlation with purity` = rho_raw) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-pathway, names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(metric = factor(metric, levels = c("Mean contribution (years)", "Spearman correlation with purity")))

p_phi_purity <- ggplot(phi_plot_df, aes(x = value, y = pathway)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = value, yend = pathway), colour = "grey70", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = value < 0), size = 2.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "#2c7bb6", "FALSE" = "#d7191c"), guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ metric, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_supp() +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())

p_phi_purity
```

## Pathways of interest: contribution against purity, per tumor

The six pathways the BRCA figures discuss (G2M checkpoint, glycolysis,
myogenesis, P53 pathway, Wnt/β-catenin, unfolded protein response) and
three immune or stromal pathways with the strongest purity dependence.
One point per tumor, coloured by PAM50, with an unadjusted linear fit and
the Spearman correlation in each panel title. Dashed line: the age
expectation (contribution of zero).

```{r, fig.width=9, fig.height=8}
poi <- intersect(params$poi_pathways, colnames(phi_b))
if (length(poi) < length(params$poi_pathways)) {
  msg("Pathways of interest not found in the contribution matrix: ",
      paste(setdiff(params$poi_pathways, colnames(phi_b)), collapse = ", "))
}

poi_long <- as.data.frame(phi_b[, poi, drop = FALSE]) %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("sample_id") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-sample_id, names_to = "pathway", values_to = "phi") %>%
  dplyr::left_join(brca_pur %>% dplyr::select(sample_id, purity, pam50), by = "sample_id")

poi_labels <- phi_purity_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(pathway %in% poi) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = sprintf("%s\nrho = %.2f, mean = %.1f yr", pathway, rho_raw, mean_phi)) %>%

poi_long <- poi_long %>%
  dplyr::left_join(poi_labels, by = "pathway") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(label = factor(label, levels = poi_labels$label[match(poi, poi_labels$pathway)]))

p_poi_purity <- ggplot(poi_long, aes(x = purity, y = phi)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +

  facet_wrap(~ label, ncol = 3, scales = "free_y") +
```

---

# Analysis 4 — BRCA main-text claims with purity in the model

## 4a. Subtype ordering

**Question.** Does the PAM50 ordering of deviation hold once purity is
accounted for?

**Why.** Subtypes differ in purity (Normal-Like lowest), so part of the
subtype spread in deviation could be composition. If purity were behind the
subtype effect, adding it would absorb that effect.

**How.** `deviation ~ PAM50 + age` and `deviation ~ PAM50 + age + purity`
on tumors with purity. Adjusted means are predictions per subtype at the
cohort mean age and, in the second model, the cohort mean purity. The
PAM50 partial F in each model shows whether the subtype effect shrinks or
grows when purity is added.

```{r}
fit_sub   <- stats::lm(deviation ~ pam50 + age_years,          data = brca_pur)
fit_sub_p <- stats::lm(deviation ~ pam50 + age_years + purity, data = brca_pur)

newdat <- tibble(
  pam50     = factor(pam50_levels, levels = pam50_levels),
  age_years = mean(brca_pur$age_years),
  purity    = mean(brca_pur$purity)
)
adj_mean <- function(fit) as.numeric(stats::predict(fit, newdata = newdat))

subtype_tbl <- tibble(
  pam50                = pam50_levels,
  n                    = as.integer(table(brca_pur$pam50)[pam50_levels]),
  mean_purity          = as.numeric(tapply(brca_pur$purity,    brca_pur$pam50, mean)[pam50_levels]),
  raw_mean_deviation   = as.numeric(tapply(brca_pur$deviation, brca_pur$pam50, mean)[pam50_levels]),
  age_adjusted         = adj_mean(fit_sub),
  age_purity_adjusted  = adj_mean(fit_sub_p)
)

knitr::kable(
  subtype_tbl, digits = 2,
  caption = "Mean deviation by PAM50 subtype: raw, adjusted for age, and adjusted for age and purity."
)
```

```{r}
pur_slope <- lm_term(fit_sub_p, "purity", scale = 0.1)
an_s  <- stats::anova(fit_sub)
an_sp <- stats::anova(fit_sub_p)

subtype_model_tbl <- tibble(
  quantity = c(
    "Purity slope per 10 pct (years), age + PAM50 adjusted",
    "Purity p-value",
    "PAM50 partial F, without purity",
    "PAM50 partial F, with purity",
    "R-squared, age + PAM50",
    "R-squared, age + PAM50 + purity"
  ),
  value = c(
    pur_slope$estimate,
    pur_slope$p_value,
    an_s["pam50", "F value"],
    an_sp["pam50", "F value"],
    summary(fit_sub)$r.squared,
    summary(fit_sub_p)$r.squared
  )
)

knitr::kable(subtype_model_tbl, digits = 4, caption = "Model terms for the two subtype models.")
```

Age-matched deviation by PAM50 subtype after purity adjustment, drawn as
in the main subtype panel. Each tumor's
deviation is adjusted to the cohort mean purity using the purity slope from
`deviation ~ PAM50 + age + purity`, which leaves the subtype and age
structure untouched and removes only the purity component. Adjacent normal
has no purity estimate and is not shown. Subtypes compared by
Kruskal-Wallis on the adjusted values, as in the main panel.

```{r, fig.width=4, fig.height=3.75}
purity_beta <- stats::coef(fit_sub_p)[["purity"]]

brca_adj <- brca_pur %>%
  dplyr::mutate(deviation_adj = deviation - purity_beta * (purity - mean(purity)))

kw_adj <- suppressWarnings(stats::kruskal.test(deviation_adj ~ pam50, data = brca_adj))
fmt_p  <- function(p) if (p < 2.2e-16) "p < 2.2e-16" else paste0("p = ", formatC(p, format = "e", digits = 2))

y_lab_pos <- max(brca_adj$deviation_adj) + 0.05 * diff(range(brca_adj$deviation_adj))

p_subtype_adj <- ggplot(brca_adj, aes(x = pam50, y = deviation_adj, fill = pam50)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey50") +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.18, alpha = 0.18, size = 0.7, colour = "grey25") +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.6, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = pam50_pal, guide = "none") +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(-60, NA)) +
  annotate("text", x = -Inf, y = y_lab_pos, label = paste("Kruskal-Wallis", fmt_p(kw_adj$p.value)),
           hjust = -0.05, vjust = 1, size = 4) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Age-matched deviation, purity-adjusted (years)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.title.y       = element_text(size = 10),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 9),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 8),
    plot.margin        = margin(10, 10, 10, 10)
  )

p_subtype_adj
```

## 4b. Overall survival: the figure's Cox forest with purity added

**Question.** Does any row of the BRCA survival forest change when purity
is added?

**Why.** The survival figure reports the aggregate deviation-survival
association, its attenuation under PAM50 adjustment, and the within-subtype
estimates. Each is a claim that purity could confound.

**How.** The figure's row set and models, TCGA only: `Surv ~ age +
deviation` on all tumors, the same with PAM50, and the same within each
subtype (a subtype is fit when it has at least 5 tumors and 2 events, as in
the figure). Every row is fit twice on the tumors with purity: as in the
figure, and with purity added. The forest uses the figure's colour (HR
direction) and shape (p below 0.05) conventions. The all-tumor row on the
full cohort, without the purity filter, is the first BRCA row of
Analysis 2.

```{r}
surv_brca_pur <- dplyr::filter(brca_pur, is.finite(os_time), !is.na(os_event), is.finite(age_years))

msg("OS-eligible BRCA tumors with purity: ", nrow(surv_brca_pur), " (", sum(surv_brca_pur$os_event), " events).")

run_forest_rows <- function(df, with_purity) {
  add <- if (with_purity) " + purity" else ""
  rows <- list()

  rows[["all"]] <- cox_term(df, paste0("Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation", add), "deviation") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "All tumors", n = nrow(df), events = sum(df$os_event))

  rows[["pam50"]] <- cox_term(df, paste0("Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation + pam50", add), "deviation") %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "All tumors (PAM50-adjusted)", n = nrow(df), events = sum(df$os_event))

  for (s in pam50_levels) {
    d <- dplyr::filter(df, pam50 == s)
    if (nrow(d) < 5 || sum(d$os_event) < 2) next
    rows[[s]] <- cox_term(d, paste0("Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation", add), "deviation") %>%
      dplyr::mutate(model = paste("Subtype:", s), n = nrow(d), events = sum(d$os_event))
  }

  dplyr::bind_rows(rows) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(adjustment = if (with_purity) "Age + purity adjusted" else "Age adjusted (as in figure)") %>%
    dplyr::select(adjustment, model, n, events, HR, CI_low, CI_high, p_value)
}

brca_forest_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  run_forest_rows(surv_brca_pur, with_purity = FALSE),
  run_forest_rows(surv_brca_pur, with_purity = TRUE)
)

knitr::kable(
  brca_forest_tbl, digits = 4,
  caption = "BRCA overall-survival forest rows (TCGA, tumors with purity): hazard ratio per +1 year of deviation, as in the figure and with purity added."
)
```

The comparison table above is the record. The panel below shows the
purity-adjusted rows alone, drawn as the TCGA-BRCA half of the main
survival forest; the unadjusted rows are the main panel.

```{r, fig.width=3.7, fig.height=2.6}
forest_df <- brca_forest_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(adjustment == "Age + purity adjusted") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    model  = factor(model, levels = rev(unique(model))),
    sig    = ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "p < 0.05", "p ≥ 0.05"),
    hr_dir = factor(
      ifelse(HR < 1, '"youth-like" deviation, increased risk', 'less "youth-like" deviation, increased risk'),
      levels = names(hr_pal)
    ),
    cohort = "TCGA-BRCA (OS), age + purity adjusted"
  )

p_brca_forest <- ggplot(forest_df, aes(x = HR, y = model, colour = hr_dir)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = CI_low, xmax = CI_high), height = 0.2, linewidth = 0.55) +
  geom_point(aes(shape = sig), size = 2.6) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey55") +
  scale_x_log10() +
  scale_shape_manual(values = c("p < 0.05" = 19, "p ≥ 0.05" = 1), name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = hr_pal, name = NULL, drop = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ cohort, ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = "HR per +1 yr of Deviation, age + purity adjusted (log scale)", y = NULL) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(
    strip.text         = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
    strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position    = "bottom",
    legend.box         = "vertical",
    legend.spacing.y   = unit(1, "pt"),
    legend.margin      = margin(0, 0, 0, 0),
    legend.text        = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.text          = element_text(size = 8),
    axis.title         = element_text(size = 9),
    plot.margin        = margin(4, 4, 4, 4)
  )

p_brca_forest
```

Purity's own hazard ratio in the two aggregate models that include it.

```{r}
brca_cox_pur_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cox_term(surv_brca_pur, "Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation + purity",         "purity", scale = 0.1) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "All tumors"),
  cox_term(surv_brca_pur, "Surv(os_time, os_event) ~ age_years + deviation + pam50 + purity", "purity", scale = 0.1) %>%
    dplyr::mutate(model = "All tumors (PAM50-adjusted)")
) %>%
  dplyr::select(model, HR, CI_low, CI_high, p_value)

knitr::kable(
  brca_cox_pur_tbl, digits = 4,
  caption = "Purity's own BRCA overall-survival hazard ratio per +10 percentage points."
)
```

## 4c. Truncating TP53 and the P53-pathway contribution

**Question.** Does the association between truncating TP53 mutations and a
more youth-like P53-pathway contribution hold with purity in the model?

**Why.** This is the main-text claim most exposed to purity. The
P53-pathway contribution correlates with purity (Analysis 3), and TP53
mutation class is not independent of purity in breast cancer, so part of
the contrast between classes could be composition, in either direction.

**How.** TP53 classes follow the figure script: cBioPortal mutation table;
truncating (nonsense, frameshift, splice site), missense, other (dropped);
tumors without a TP53 entry are wild type; when a patient has several
mutations the highest-impact class wins, and every tumor profile of a
patient carries that patient's class. The unit of analysis is the patient:
a patient with more than one tumor profile is represented once, by the mean
of their P53-pathway contributions (PAM50, purity, and TP53 class are
patient-level and identical across a patient's profiles). This matters here
because several replicated patients fall into the small mutation classes.
As in the figure, all five tumor PAM50 subtypes are kept and the model
adjusts for PAM50. Estimated marginal means per class and each class
against wild type with Dunnett adjustment, as in the figure. Three fits:
all TCGA patients (TCGA-only model), patients with purity, and patients
with purity plus the purity term, with the marginal means taken at the
cohort mean purity.

```{r}
tp53_raw <- utils::read.delim(
  params$tp53_tsv, sep = "\t", quote = "", check.names = FALSE, stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

# cBioPortal exports can carry duplicate column names; keep only the three columns used
tp53_cols <- c("Gene", "Sample ID", "Mutation Type")
stopifnot(all(tp53_cols %in% colnames(tp53_raw)))
tp53_raw <- tp53_raw[, match(tp53_cols, colnames(tp53_raw)), drop = FALSE]

trunc_classes <- c("Nonsense_Mutation", "Frame_Shift_Del", "Frame_Shift_Ins", "Splice_Site")
miss_classes  <- c("Missense_Mutation")

tp53_by_patient <- tp53_raw %>%
  dplyr::filter(Gene == "TP53") %>%
  dplyr::transmute(
    patient = substr(`Sample ID`, 1, 12),
    class   = dplyr::case_when(
      `Mutation Type` %in% trunc_classes ~ "Truncating",
      `Mutation Type` %in% miss_classes  ~ "Missense",
      TRUE                               ~ "Other_Mut"
    )
  ) %>%
  dplyr::group_by(patient) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    tp53 = dplyr::case_when(
      any(class == "Truncating") ~ "Truncating",
      any(class == "Missense")   ~ "Missense",
      TRUE                       ~ "Other_Mut"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

p53_col <- grep("^p53", colnames(purity_data$phi_brca), ignore.case = TRUE, value = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(p53_col) == 1)

# one row per tumor profile, every profile carrying its patient's TP53 class
tp53_profiles <- brca %>%
  dplyr::mutate(p53_phi = as.numeric(purity_data$phi_brca[sample_id, p53_col])) %>%
  dplyr::left_join(tp53_by_patient, by = "patient") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tp53 = ifelse(is.na(tp53), "WT", tp53)) %>%
  dplyr::filter(tp53 != "Other_Mut")

# PAM50, purity, and TP53 class must not vary within a patient
stopifnot(all(tp53_profiles %>% dplyr::count(patient, pam50, tp53) %>% dplyr::count(patient) %>% dplyr::pull(n) == 1))
stopifnot(all(tp53_profiles %>% dplyr::group_by(patient) %>% dplyr::summarise(k = dplyr::n_distinct(purity)) %>% dplyr::pull(k) == 1))

# one row per patient: mean P53 contribution across that patient's profiles
tp53_df <- tp53_profiles %>%
  dplyr::group_by(patient, pam50, tp53, purity) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(p53_phi = mean(p53_phi), n_profiles = dplyr::n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tp53 = factor(tp53, levels = c("WT", "Missense", "Truncating")))

tp53_df_pur <- dplyr::filter(tp53_df, !is.na(purity))

msg("TP53 analysis: ", nrow(tp53_profiles), " tumor profiles from ", nrow(tp53_df), " patients; ",
    sum(tp53_df$n_profiles > 1), " patients with more than one profile.")

knitr::kable(
  tp53_df %>%
    dplyr::group_by(tp53) %>%
    dplyr::summarise(
      patients            = dplyr::n(),
      profiles            = sum(n_profiles),
      with_purity         = sum(!is.na(purity)),
      mean_purity         = mean(purity, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_p53_phi        = mean(p53_phi),
      .groups = "drop"
    ),
  digits = 3,
  caption = "BRCA patients by TP53 class (other mutation classes excluded), with the number of tumor profiles they contribute, mean purity, and mean P53-pathway contribution."
)
```

```{r}
tp53_specs <- list(
  list(label = "All patients (TCGA-only model)",         data = tp53_df,     f = p53_phi ~ tp53 + pam50),
  list(label = "Patients with purity",                   data = tp53_df_pur, f = p53_phi ~ tp53 + pam50),
  list(label = "Patients with purity, purity-adjusted",  data = tp53_df_pur, f = p53_phi ~ tp53 + pam50 + purity)
)

emm_rows <- list()
con_rows <- list()

for (s in tp53_specs) {
  fit <- stats::lm(s$f, data = s$data)
  emm <- emmeans::emmeans(fit, ~ tp53)
  con <- emmeans::contrast(emm, method = "trt.vs.ctrl", ref = "WT", adjust = "dunnettx")

  emm_rows[[s$label]] <- as.data.frame(confint(emm)) %>%
    tibble::as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::transmute(panel = s$label, tp53, emmean, lower.CL, upper.CL, n = nrow(s$data))

  con_rows[[s$label]] <- as.data.frame(summary(con, infer = TRUE)) %>%
    tibble::as_tibble() %>%
    dplyr::transmute(panel = s$label, contrast, estimate, lower.CL, upper.CL, p_value = p.value, n = nrow(s$data))
}

tp53_emm_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(emm_rows)
tp53_tbl     <- dplyr::bind_rows(con_rows)

knitr::kable(
  tp53_tbl, digits = 4,
  caption = "Shift in P53-pathway contribution (years) for each TP53 class against wild type, PAM50-adjusted estimated marginal means with Dunnett adjustment, without and with purity. Negative values are more youth-like."
)

tp53_pur_tbl <- lm_term(stats::lm(p53_phi ~ tp53 + pam50 + purity, data = tp53_df_pur), "purity", scale = 0.1)

knitr::kable(
  tp53_pur_tbl, digits = 4,
  caption = "Purity's own effect on the P53-pathway contribution (years per +10 percentage points), with TP53 class and PAM50 in the model."
)
```

The TP53 panel with purity in the model, drawn as the TCGA-BRCA facet of
the main panel. The three-fit table above is the
record; the unadjusted estimate is the main panel.

```{r, fig.width=3.25, fig.height=3.75}
tp53_levels <- c("WT", "Missense", "Truncating")
adj_label   <- "Patients with purity, purity-adjusted"

emm_plot_df <- tp53_emm_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(panel == adj_label) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(tp53 = factor(as.character(tp53), levels = tp53_levels),
                panel = "TCGA-BRCA, PAM50 + purity adjusted")

# significance brackets positioned above the CI tops, staggered, as in the main figure
ci_top  <- max(emm_plot_df$upper.CL)
ci_span <- max(emm_plot_df$upper.CL) - min(emm_plot_df$lower.CL)

annot_df <- tp53_tbl %>%
  dplyr::filter(panel == adj_label) %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    tp53       = sub(" - WT$", "", contrast),
    p_label    = ifelse(p_value < 0.001, "p < 0.001", sprintf("p = %.3f", p_value)),
    y.position = ci_top + ci_span * (0.10 + 0.18 * (dplyr::row_number() - 1)),
    group1     = "WT",
    group2     = tp53,
    panel      = "TCGA-BRCA, PAM50 + purity adjusted"
  )

p_tp53 <- ggplot(emm_plot_df, aes(x = tp53, y = emmean)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = lower.CL, ymax = upper.CL), width = 0.15, linewidth = 0.8, colour = "#7b3294") +
  geom_point(size = 3.5, colour = "#7b3294") +
  ggpubr::stat_pvalue_manual(
    annot_df,
    label       = "p_label",
    xmin        = "group1",
    xmax        = "group2",
    y.position  = "y.position",
    tip.length  = 0.01,
    inherit.aes = FALSE
  ) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel, nrow = 1) +
  labs(x = "TP53 mutation class", y = "Emmean P53 Pathway Dev. (years, adj.)") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    strip.text         = element_text(size = 10, face = "bold"),
    strip.background   = element_rect(fill = "grey95", colour = NA),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x        = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
    axis.text.y        = element_text(size = 8)
  )

p_tp53
```
